newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Controversial Indonesian priest wins rights award.
newsitem.headline: Controversial Indonesian priest wins rights award.

text.p: An Indonesian Catholic priest, under investigation for harbouring activists accused of subversion, has won a prestigious human rights award, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Friday.

The Jakarta-based Centre for Human Rights Studies (Yapusham) announced on Thursday that Jesuit priest Father Ignatius Sandyawan Sumardi would be presented with the Yap Thiam Hien award on December 10 for his solid commitment to the protection of human rights.
Award judge Mardjono Reksodiputro said Sandyawan, 38, had shown his commitment by helping street children, workers and the homeless through his work with the Jakarta Social Institute.
"He risked his own safety to protect the victims of the July 27 riots and those whose lives were in danger at that time," Mardjono added.
Sandyawan was accused of sheltering three members of the leftist People's Democratic Party (PRD), in the wake of the July riots in Jakarta.
The government and military have blamed the PRD for instigating the riots.
The priest was also the secretary of a team of volunteers set up to assist victims of the riots.

Todung Mulya Lubis, the human rights centre's executive director, said Sandyawan knew that helping people who were scared by the military's shoot-on-the-spot order was risky, but he had not let fear override his commitment to human rights.
Sandyawan is still under police investigation after he admitted to harbouring the leader of the PRD, Budiman Sudjatmiko and other PRD activists.
The activists approached Sandyawan after the riots and sought shelter, fearing the military would shoot them.
The activists were arrested on August 11 at the house of Sandyawan's brother in East Jakarta and have been charged with subversion which carries the death penalty in Indonesia.
The riots on July 27 were regarded as the worst unrest in the city for more than two decades. At least five people died and 23 were reported as missing.
